definitions.explanation: A word or expression that was used in older forms of Japanese but is no longer commonly used in modern speech.
The classical form of Japanese as used in literature before the modern period, studied in Japanese schools as a subject.

examples.japanese: この{言葉|ことば}は{古語|こご}なので、{今|いま}ではほとんど{使|つか}われない。
examples.english: This word is archaic, so it is hardly ever used anymore.

examples.japanese: {古語|こご}の{意味|いみ}を{調|しら}べるには{古語|こご}{辞典|じてん}が{便利|べんり}だ。
examples.english: A classical Japanese dictionary is useful for looking up the meanings of archaic words.

examples.japanese: {高校|こうこう}で{古語|こご}を{習|なら}う。
examples.english: We study classical Japanese in high school.

examples.japanese: {古語|こご}の{文法|ぶんぽう}は{現代語|げんだいご}とかなり{違|ちが}う。
examples.english: Classical Japanese grammar is quite different from modern Japanese.

examples.japanese: {古語|こご}を{学|まな}ぶと、{古典|こてん}{文学|ぶんがく}を{原文|げんぶん}で{読|よ}む{楽|たの}しさがわかるようになる。
examples.english: When you study classical Japanese, you come to understand the joy of reading classical literature in the original.

notes:
USAGE:
In Japanese schools, {古語|こご} is studied as part of the {国語|こくご} (Japanese language) curriculum, primarily at the high school level. Students learn to read classical texts like {源氏物語|げんじものがたり} and {枕草子|まくらのそうし}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {古語|こご}{辞典|じてん}: classical Japanese dictionary
- {古語|こご}の{文法|ぶんぽう}: classical grammar
- {古語|こご}の{意味|いみ}: meaning of an archaic word

SIMILAR WORDS:
{古語|こご} refers specifically to old words or classical language. {古典|こてん} means "classics" and refers to classical works of literature. {古文|こぶん} means "classical text" and overlaps with {古語|こご} in school contexts but emphasizes the written texts themselves.
